headline: Congress gives a private foundation more time to build a memorial in Washington, DC, honoring emergency medical services workers.
what_it_does: This law renews the National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Foundation's permission to build a monument in Washington, DC, honoring the service of emergency medical services. The new permission lasts seven years from the date the law was enacted.
when_it_takes_effect: Took effect when signed on September 11, 2026; the permission to build the memorial expires seven years later, around September 11, 2033.
